objective: Introduce Slayer Prime as the bounded enforcement control plane beneath Guardian authorization and harden its distributed-safety boundary against duplicate execution, restart resurrection, split-brain writes, and Prime state loss.

conflicts.originalConflict: Historical Slayer documentation described Slayer as Level 1 and referenced the stale core/slayer path.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Normalize Slayer to Level 2 enforcement/diagnostic responsibility, use the current core/slayers path, and make Slayer Prime the explicit enforcement subsystem.

conflicts.originalConflict: Legacy Slayer behavior mixed detection/case creation with the intended enforcement boundary.
conflicts.proposedResolution: Keep the existing Slayer swarm for detection and investigation while introducing Prime for authorized containment mutation, fencing, execution receipts, and postcondition proof.

changes: Added Slayer Prime contracts for incidents, evidence, action intents, authorization grants, action leases, containment proofs, and enforcement receipts.
Added evidence quorum with freshness, trust, and independent evidence-class requirements.
Added action policy with graduated scope and Guardian/Human authorization binding.
Added separate Slayer action lease with monotonic fencing token.
Added transactional enforcement executor with authoritative postcondition verification.
Added executable REVOKE_LEASE adapter backed by the existing LeaseManager.
Rejected unsupported physical enforcement actions instead of simulating success.
Wired canonical Slayer observations into Slayer Prime.
Wired Slayer Prime into SlayerEngine lifecycle and parallelized specialized patrol execution.
Added dedicated Slayer Prime tests.
Added durable Prime incident, intent, receipt, leadership, and action-lease state-store abstraction.
Added unique process-incarnation identity and monotonic leadership epochs for split-brain resistance.
Added deterministic cross-replica intent deduplication and pre-execution EXECUTING marker.
Added worker lease fencing tokens and atomic fenced release for built-in lease repositories.
Retain action reservation across ambiguous adapter outcomes to prevent immediate blind replay.
Updated Slayer hierarchy documentation and added Slayer Prime .okf contract.
Added durable Prime state-store abstraction with in-memory, single-host disk, and shared Mongo implementations.
Added Prime leadership lease with unique process-incarnation identity and monotonic leadership epochs.
Added deterministic cross-replica action-intent deduplication and shared monotonic action fencing.
Added current-leader and current-action-lease checks immediately before mutation.
Added leadership-epoch protection against stale incident state overwrites.
Added Mongo index-readiness gating and duplicate-key handling for election/intent races.
Added distributed hardening tests for restart takeover, stale writes, duplicate intents, stale action fences, and monotonic action tokens.
Hardened leadership validation to require exact epoch equality, preventing a stale generation from acting after a successful renewal.
Added dedicated exact-generation fencing regression coverage.
notes: No floor topology or sovereign authority change was introduced.
Slayer Prime is an enforcement boundary, not a cognitive authority; Ascalon/AER cannot grant Prime authority.
Only REVOKE_LEASE is currently backed by a real runtime adapter.
FENCE, ISOLATE, TERMINATE, FLOOR_HALT, and FACTORY_HALT remain adapter-gated and are not claimed as physically implemented.
Repository CI validation is expected to run from the PR head and must be checked before merge.
Prime distributed coordination is implemented through the state-store abstraction; InMemory remains test/offline, Disk is single-host recovery, Mongo is the shared multi-replica path.
Legacy LeaseManager still lacks an atomic worker-resource fencing-token release contract; REVOKE_LEASE uses optional resource fencing when available and retains owner/status checks otherwise.
Durable cross-process observation delivery/replay remains a separate required wave because the current DurableEventBus is process-local.
